text:
anika: Heads-up — canary rollout of NVIDIA driver 572 to canary pool failed in ap-southeast-1 and eu-west-1. Several nodes are stuck in early boot, DKMS compile errors and initramfs waiting on nvidia modules. Attaching short logs. :rotating_light:

kevin: Can you paste the DKMS error? Is this only new AMIs or also old images getting the driver installed?

anika: Quick snippet from one of the nodes — DKMS build fails during post-install:
```
DKMS: building module for kernel 5.15.0-1023-aws
make -C /lib/modules/5.15.0-1023-aws/build M=/var/lib/dkms/nvidia/572/build
make[1]: Entering directory '/usr/src/linux-headers-5.15.0-1023-aws'
  CC [M]  /var/lib/dkms/nvidia/572/build/nvidia.ko
/usr/bin/ld: error: undefined reference to symbol 'module_layout'
collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status
make[1]: *** [Makefile:1611: /var/lib/dkms/nvidia/572/build/nvidia.ko] Error 1
DKMS: ERROR: Failed to install module nvidia/572 for kernel 5.15.0-1023-aws
```

anika: Also dracut logs show `Waiting for device: nvidia0` and the initramfs times out so node never finishes boot. This seems correlated with kernel headers not matching the running kernel on some of our AMIs.

maria: Ugh. Is this the canary image we baked last night? I thought DKMS compile step was in the pipeline.

kevin: The pipeline ran but only on the new builder AMI. Looks like some older host images in the canary pool still have custom kernel packages (we ship a bespoke low-latency config) so headers diverge. DKMS unpacks and tries to build against wrong headers.

jonathan: Impact: currently about 18% of our GPU capacity in ap-southeast-1 and 12% in eu-west-1 are unavailable because those nodes are stuck in provisioning. That’s spiking queuing for Dedicated customers — we have customers hitting rate limits and some model-hosted tasks timing out. Cost impact: we had to spin up 30 CPU-only fallbacks — doubling short-term bill for those jobs.

li: FYI the dedicated pool in ap-southeast has two reserved nodes in that canary group; they’re stuck too. We should flag this to Sales/Success if SLAs might be affected.

ops-bot: [alert] node-provisioning-failure ap-southeast-1 count=12 eu-west-1 count=9 — common failure: dkms-build-failed, initramfs-timeout

kevin: Short-term mitigation options: 1) stop the rollout and rollback driver upgrade on remaining canary hosts, 2) mark affected nodes as unschedulable and attempt safe reboot, or 3) boot nodes with `modprobe.blacklist=nvidia` to allow the node to join the cluster (no GPU) while we rebuild AMIs. Thoughts?

maria: I prefer rollback on remaining hosts and create a new canary image with explicit kernel-header pinning. Booting with `modprobe.blacklist=nvidia` is ok as a last resort but it'll force job fallbacks — not great for Dedicated customers.

anika: Agreed. I'm going to stop the rollout in the controller now and add a rollback flag.

sre-oncall: If you need a quick patch on existing nodes, you can try creating the missing header symlink: `ln -s /usr/src/linux-headers-5.15.0-1023-aws /lib/modules/5.15.0-1023-aws/build` — that will let DKMS complete on some images, but it's fragile and we should only use it on non-customer-dedicated nodes.

kevin: Good call. Also add an explicit DKMS compile step to the bake pipeline that runs inside the final AMI (not just the builder). We should fail the bake if `dkms build` or `make` fails.

jonathan: Ops/Finance: estimate of incremental cost from fallback CPU instances so far ~ $3.1k/day if not resolved by EOD. Need to decide whether to preemptively expand capacity in another region to shift load — that has cross-region egress/cost implications.

li: I'll message PS and Sales with a heads-up and SLAs potentially affected.

anika: Plan agreed: 1) stop rollout (done), 2) rollback driver on any remaining nodes, 3) bake new AMI with pinned headers + DKMS compile step + test boot verification, 4) re-run canary in a smaller pool with nodes that match kernel package set, 5) add postmortem/runbook. I'll open a follow-up ticket.

kevin: Also add a kubelet-start gating check in the bake that ensures `nvidia-smi` loads without errors for a tiny smoke workload.

ops-bot: [action] rollout-stopped by anika at 1972104358

sre-oncall: I'm going to patch two non-dedicated nodes with the header symlink to get extra capacity for CI until we have the new AMI.

maria: Thanks everyone. When you open the ticket, include the exact failing logs and the list of affected instances so Support can triage customer impact.

kevin: noted. I'll also add a checklist for verifying kernel header parity across all our AMIs so this doesn't slip again.

anika: ack :thumbsup:
